column.text: Bitcoin is down 3.99% and the ETF tape is confirming it. Thursday's (12 Nov) BTC ETF outflows came in at −$284.1M, lifting the seven-day net to −$1647.4M. Ether logged −$70.5M on Thursday and −$541.4M over seven days, while SOL shed −$1.9M on the day and −$53.9M over the week. Liquidations reached $238M in the session, and longs were the ones getting forced out. The desk reads this as a long squeeze, not clean selling. Daily RSI sits at 25.14 for BTC and 20.75 for SOL, deep in oversold territory, yet price keeps sliding because leveraged longs are being flushed. Hyperliquid whale positioning shows net short exposure of $545M in BTC, $302M in ETH and $79M in SOL, so the crowd leans the same way the tape does. Fear & Greed reads 20, Extreme Fear, which makes any bounce vulnerable to a squeeze. The regime is RISK_OFF. Continuation shorts ride momentum, and dollar liquidity is flat, so there is no macro wind to lean on either way. Longs need a real mechanism: deeply negative funding, a capitulation print, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown. An oversold reading alone does not qualify. Headlines add pressure too, with the Fed's Collins warning rates may need to rise more than expected. Until price reclaims key resistance, the path of least resistance stays lower. Watch whether ETF outflows slow before anyone calls a bottom.
